summary.text: 水 depicts flowing water: a central current with marks for droplets. Its common meaning is “water.”

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph pictures flowing water. The historical account in Shuowen adds a cosmological explanation, which is distinct from this pictorial analysis.

history.text: Oracle-script forms vary in their side marks, while bronze and Warring States forms retain the flowing-water picture. The selected oracle-script and Western Zhou bronze-script images show these forms as modern vector redrawings, not photographs of artifacts.

Shuowen preserves a Han-era gloss and cosmological account of water. Its explanation is a historical interpretation of the word and graph, not evidence that the graph was formed from separate components.

uncertainties.text: The supplied reconstructions and proposed comparisons for the spoken word 水 differ and remain unresolved; none indicates a phonetic component in this pictograph.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone examples; individual dates unresolved
senses.text: The cited oracle-bone examples are reported for water or flooding; water is the character’s basic meaning.
The common current meaning is “water.” Other glosses include liquid, lotion, and juice, but their chronology is not established.
The compound 水準 is reported with the meaning “leveling instrument.” This use is not dated in the cited account.
水準 is also reported with the abstract sense “standard” or “level,” described as developing from the instrument sense. Neither stage is dated in the cited account.
A bronze inscription is reported to use 水 to write the different word 乞, “request.” This is graph borrowing, not a meaning change from “water” to “request.”
One reported oracle-bone use has been read as a verb involving leveling ground with water or washing a temple. Its reading and relation to the noun “water” remain unresolved.

developments.text: The abstract sense “standard” or “level” is described as developing from the leveling-instrument sense, though the transition is not dated.

The graph was reportedly reused for 乞, “request,” on the proposed basis that the words sounded alike or similarly. The historical sound match is unverified; the old name of the pictured water and a reconstruction comparison for both words are not established here.

limitations.text: Individual oracle-bone examples and the stages of 水準 are not dated in the cited accounts. The disputed verbal use’s relation to the ordinary water noun is unresolved.
The proposed sound-based explanation for writing 乞 with 水 is not confirmed by a historical comparison of the two words’ pronunciations.

items.period: Shang dynasty oracle-script style; Commons page cites source form 甲903 合34165 but does not provide a specific date for that item
items.tradition: Oracle-bone script; modern vector redraw, not an artifact photograph
items.caption: Oracle-script 水 has a winding central stroke with short marks on either side, matching the picture of flowing water with droplets.
items.alt: Black oracle-script glyph with a winding central stroke and four separate side marks, two on each side.
items.selection_reason: Its visible structure illustrates the reported pictorial analysis of 水 as flowing water; it is the clearest candidate for explaining the character’s formation.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public-domain dedication as stated on the exact Commons file page; its source note attributes the form to the Sinica database.

items.period: Early Western Zhou, according to the Commons description’s source note for 沈子它簋蓋
items.tradition: Western Zhou bronze inscription style; modern vector redraw, not a photograph of the bronze vessel
items.caption: This bronze-script form of 水 also has a winding central stroke and separate side marks, preserving the flowing-water picture.
items.alt: Black bronze-script glyph with a long winding central stroke and four separate side marks.
items.selection_reason: It offers a useful comparison showing the flowing-water motif in a bronze-script form, which the cited analysis says retains that picture.
items.rights: Public domain, as stated for the vector representation on the exact Commons file page.

limitations.text: These are modern vector redrawings of historical script forms, not photographs of the original inscriptions; the underlying artifacts were not inspected, and individual dates for the cited oracle examples are not established here.
